page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 937 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The processor achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (34.34 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.1 GB/sec). However, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks are comparatively limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression both falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth read-only tests also register as weak, though large block write bandwidth and Passmark memory scores maintain average ratings.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe storage and DDR5 memory relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it a specialized option for workloads requiring fast local storage access rather than raw multi-core compute scaling. The presence of advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), supports specialized vector and matrix operations. This hardware profile is suited for database operations, local caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks, while being less optimal for highly parallelized multi-threaded compute workloads or memory-bandwidth-bound applications.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz and a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD. Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 and strong single-threaded compression performance. However, multi-core scaling and memory read bandwidth are relatively weak. The instance supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Qualitatively, the i7i.xlarge provides high storage and memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for database operations, localized caching, and single-threaded processing tasks where local NVMe speed is prioritized over multi-threaded compute scaling.
